newsitem.title: USA: Clinton sees "new and hopeful" signs on budget.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sees "new and hopeful" signs on budget.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday he saw "new and hopeful" signs on the chances of reaching a balanced budget deal with Congress and invited the leaders of the congressional budget committees to meet him on Wednesday.

"We have to seize this opportunity to pass a bipartisan agreement to balance the budget," Clinton told reporters at the White House. "There are now some new and hopeful signs that we are in a position to do that."

"Yesterday, the Republican leaders showed me flexibility on tax cuts and economic assumptions. This new flexibility is a very positive sign," Clinton said, apparently referring to House Speaker Newt Gingrich's endorsing the idea of putting off a major tax cut in order to reach a balanced budget deal.

"They move us closer than ever to the point where we can reach an agreement on a balanced budget that is good for the American people," Clinton told reporters in his upstairs White House residence, where he is recovering from knee surgery.

Clinton said he was taking three steps to move the budget process forward -- inviting the budget committee leaders to meet him on Wednesday, asking his budget team to hold talks with congressional budget leaders during the congressional recess, and asking them to report back afterwards at the White House.
Asked if he were willing to be flexible on his own tax cut proposal, Clinton did not commit himself but replied: "On all these issues I have to show flexibility, they have to show flexibility."
